messages:
maria.lee: Quick question — a customer wants every audit webhook payload encrypted with their KMS key before delivery. Will that break our current webhook signature validation flow?

alex.k: Short answer: yes, if we encrypt the payload after we compute the HMAC. The recipient needs the plain payload to verify the signature.

maria.lee: Right. They want envelope encryption with their key (AWS KMS) so events at rest + in transit are protected. They also expect Datadog/Splunk connectors to ingest events.

alex.k: Two approaches I can think of: 1) Sign-then-encrypt: we HMAC the plaintext, encrypt the whole package, and deliver — recipient must decrypt then verify. 2) Encrypt-then-sign: sign the ciphertext with a separate key so recipient can verify signature before decrypting. Both require the recipient to have decrypt permissions / keys.

kevin: For most webhook consumers (Datadog, Splunk HTTP intake) they can't decrypt. So encrypted webhook payloads will be incompatible unless they run a decrypt proxy.

anya: Could we instead keep webhook plaintext but use mTLS + HMAC and document S3 KMS as the encrypted-at-rest option? Customer prefers KMS-managed keys under their account though.

alex.k: We already support S3 exports with SSE-KMS using customer key arn (created in their account) — that meets most compliance asks. For webhooks, two realistic roadmap options: A) Add "encryptedEnvelope" mode requiring customer-provided decrypt endpoint (or proxy) B) Provide a managed-decrypt connector (only available for Dedicated/Private).

maria.lee: From product side, they'd prefer option B if possible — fewer integration steps for customers. But that implies we store the key material or have permission to call their KMS (via cross-account IAM). Need security opinion.

sec-bot: reminder: any solution that involves Redwood calling customer KMS needs thorough IAM scoping, audit logging, and explicit consent in contract. Also add rate limits and retry semantics to avoid accidental key misuse.

kevin: Implementation notes: if we support calling customer KMS to decrypt envelopes before forwarding to downstream SIEMs, we should not persist plaintext except in transit. That means ephemeral memory only and strict scrub logs. Also need to extend audit schema with encryption metadata.

maria.lee: What fields are we thinking for schema?

alex.k: Proposal for webhook headers and event payload additions:

- HTTP headers: `X-RW-Signature-v1` (HMAC of plaintext or ciphertext depending on mode), `X-RW-Encrypted: true|false`, `X-RW-Encryption-Mode: envelope|sse`, `X-RW-KMS-Key: arn:aws:kms:...` (only for envelope)

- Event body: add top-level `encryption_metadata` object with `key_id`, `algorithm`, `iv` (if applicable), and `encoding` (base64).

Example plaintext event (before encryption):

```
{
  "actor": "user:alice",
  "action": "api_key.rotate",
  "resource": "project/1234",
  "ts": "2026-03-10T15:23:45Z",
  "details": { "old_key_id": "k-abc" }
}
```

Example envelope payload (what we would send if envelope mode):

```
{
  "encryption_metadata": {
    "key_id": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01",
    "algorithm": "aws:kms+aes-256-gcm",
    "encoding": "base64"
  },
  "ciphertext": "BASE64_AES_GCM_PAYLOAD",
  "signature": "hmac-sha256=..."  // if we sign the ciphertext
}
```

kevin: If we sign ciphertext, receivers that can't decrypt can still verify authenticity, but they can't inspect the event content for routing rules. SIEMs (Datadog/Splunk) generally expect plain JSON, so they'd need a decrypting forwarder.

anya: For onboarding docs we should:
- Outline supported delivery modes (plain webhook w/ HMAC + TLS, S3 SSE-KMS, SIEM connectors)
- Call out that envelope-encrypted webhooks require either a customer decrypt endpoint or Redwood-managed decrypt (Dedicated/Private only)
- Provide example IAM role policy for cross-account KMS decrypt if customer wants us to call their KMS

maria.lee: Can someone draft the IAM policy snippet we should include? Keep it minimal (Decrypt permissions only and condition on resource).

alex.k: Draft policy (to include in onboarding doc):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDCOWD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-kms-client" },
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": { "kms:EncryptionContext:purpose": "redwood-audit-forwarding" }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

kevin: We'll also need to extend our audit logging coverage to record when we call customer KMS and whether decrypt succeeded/failed, without recording plaintext. Minimal log entry: timestamp, key_id, call_status, error_code.

sec-bot: compliance check: log retention for decrypt calls must be configurable per-customer and included in contract for Private/Dedicated. Also add a flag to disable decrypt logging entirely for high-sensitivity customers.

maria.lee: OK. Action items:
- alex.k: write RFC for webhook encryption modes + schema additions, include sample headers and payload, and threat model (due EOW).
- kevin: prototype server-side decrypt flow for a webhook -> decrypt -> forward to Datadog (no persistence) and measure latency impact.
- anya: update onboarding doc with IAM policy snippet, supported modes, and checklist for customer steps.

alex.k: noted. I'll also add compatibility matrix: which SIEMs can accept encrypted events natively (none), which need forwarder, and recommended patterns.

maria.lee: Thanks. If we decide to support customer KMS calls, security sign-off will be required. @sec-bot add checklist item. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: Added security checklist item: `KMS cross-account decrypt review` to the ticket.

anya: One small edge-case: customers using HSM-backed keys with external key stores may require on-prem connectors. We'll note that in docs and recommend Redwood Private.

kevin: End-to-end test plan suggestion:
- Create test customer with KMS key and cross-account role
- Send audit event, request envelope mode, verify decrypt path and signature verification
- Run Datadog ingestion via local forwarder to show latency and correctness

maria.lee: Cool. I'll convert this thread into a ticket and assign. Thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
